summary: Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues tourist visas through its online eVisa portal and on arrival at Iran's international airports, and its portal lists the countries whose citizens enter without a visa. US, UK and Canadian citizens need a visa before travel according to their governments' advice (the UK Foreign Office says British passport holders need an organised tour or a sponsor in Iran), and Iran's visa portal says it may refuse visas to some nationalities for political and diplomatic considerations without naming them.

GB.notes: Iran's MFA visa portal says some types of visa for the citizens of some countries can be applied for only in person through an Iranian embassy, without naming the countries. The UK Foreign Office says the Iranian Embassy has told it that, to get a visa with a British passport, you must either apply as part of an organised tour or have a sponsor in Iran; check with the Iranian Embassy in the UK. Iran's Interests Section in Washington also says UK citizens must apply only through travel agencies or their host in Iran, and lists a UK tourist-visa fee of USD 225 (USD 338 expedited) for applications made there.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Iran entry requirements (Applying for a visa)

US.notes: The US State Department says U.S. passports are valid for travel to Iran and a tourist visa is required except for Kish Island, and advises against all travel to Iran (Level 4: Do Not Travel). Iran's Interests Section in Washington says US citizens must apply only through a travel agency or their host in Iran; the visa is issued electronically after the passport is mailed to the Interests Section.

fee.notes: EUR 50 is what Iran's embassy in Berlin charges German passport holders for a single-entry tourist visa (EUR 75 if urgent, issued the same day or within 72 hours), plus a EUR 10 travel-insurance fee. Fees differ by nationality and by the mission that issues the visa; visas collected on arrival are paid in euros at airport bank terminals. The embassy says visas applied for through the agencies it lists are usually issued within at most 10 to 12 days of the application being handed in.

source.name: Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Berlin — Visa and visa fees (Visatarif für Inhaber deutscher Reisepässe)

passportValidity.text: Your passport must have at least six months' validity beyond your travel date. The UK Foreign Office says that if your passport has stamps from Israel or other countries' border crossing points with Israel, you may be refused entry to Iran.

source.name: Iran eVisa — MFA visa portal (English: Important Tips, Passport Expiration)

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you need a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Iran only if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Iran entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Polio
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says that if you are coming from a polio-affected country, you need a certificate proving you have had a polio vaccine.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Iran entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: Iran's embassy in Berlin adds a EUR 10 travel-insurance fee to every visa fee it charges; no official source we could read says whether the eVisa or the visa on arrival requires it.

source.name: Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Berlin — visa fees and procedure

onwardTicket.text: No official source states an onward-ticket requirement. The MFA eVisa application asks for your travel itinerary only if you have already made travel arrangements.

source.name: Iran MFA eVisa — How to complete the application

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Iran. The UK government says non-Iranian debit and cash cards will not work in Iran.

source.name: UK FCDO — Iran travel advice

currencyLimits.text: No Iranian source we could read states a cash-declaration threshold: the customs administration's site (irica.ir) did not answer and the MFA eVisa portal is silent. The US State Department lists currency restrictions on amounts over EUR 10,000 on entry and over EUR 5,000 on exit.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Iran international travel information

notes: The UK government says it is illegal to import, sell, manufacture or drink alcohol in Iran, and that importing pork products is illegal.
The UK government says you need permission from the Iranian authorities to import or use drones or satellite phones; using them without permission is illegal and can lead to arrest.

Canada's travel advice says travellers have been denied entry because their passports bore an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a crossing on the border with Israel.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Iran's economy is exclusively cash-based: credit cards are not accepted and ATMs serve only local bank accounts. The UK government adds that non-Iranian debit cards will not work, that changing money on the street is illegal, and that euros and US dollars are more commonly accepted at exchange offices than pounds sterling.

safety.text: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments all advise against all travel to Iran, citing the volatile security situation, regional conflict and the risk of arbitrary detention, particularly for dual nationals. The UK government also reports attacks and robberies targeted at foreign nationals and tourists.

source.name: UK FCDO — Iran travel advice
IEC World Plugs (International Electrotechnical Commission) — plug types, voltage and frequency by location

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says the weather is very dry and hot from May to October, when dust storms can occur, and that the rainy season runs from November to March, sometimes with flash flooding.

idp.text: Iran is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Iran is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. No official source we could read states whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, or for how long a foreign licence may be used.

tips.text: The UK government says Islamic dress codes are strictly enforced: in public, women must cover their heads with a headscarf and wear trousers or a floor-length skirt with a long-sleeved tunic or coat reaching mid-thigh or knee, and men should wear long trousers and long-sleeved shirts.

Iran's MFA visa portal says some types of visa for the citizens of some countries can be applied for only in person at an Iranian embassy, without naming the countries. The UK Foreign Office says the Iranian Embassy has told it that British passport holders must apply as part of an organised tour or have a sponsor in Iran. Canada's travel advice says a tourist visa is required, and the US State Department advises against all travel to Iran.

Iran's MFA describes visa on arrival at Iran's international airports and asks travellers to apply online at least two days before travel and to hand a printed copy of the grant notice to the visa-on-arrival counter; the fee is paid in euros at the airport's bank terminals.
Australia's Smartraveller says Iran does not recognise dual nationality and that foreign and dual nationals are at high risk of arbitrary detention or arrest, without guaranteed consular access.
The UK government says non-Iranian debit cards will not work in Iran, changing money on the street is illegal, and exchange offices accept euros and US dollars more commonly than pounds sterling.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iran?
faq.answer: Unless your country is on Iran's visa-waiver lists, yes. Iran's MFA says all types of visa can be applied for through its online portal, evisa.mfa.ir, and describes a visa on arrival at Iran's international airports, but it also says some visas for the citizens of some countries are issued only in person at an embassy and that some nationalities may be refused, without naming them. Its portal lists the countries whose citizens enter visa-free, among them Turkey, Azerbaijan, Armenia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, China, Iraq and Oman, and 27 more whose ordinary passport holders may stay 15 days for tourism once every six months. US, UK, Canadian, Australian and German citizens need a visa according to their own governments; the UK Foreign Office says British passport holders must apply as part of an organised tour or have a sponsor in Iran.

faq.question: Can Americans visit Iran?
faq.answer: US passports are valid for travel to Iran, the US State Department says, but it advises against all travel there (Level 4: Do Not Travel) and says a tourist visa is required. No official page we could read states a guided-tour or authorization-code rule for US passport holders. For British passport holders, the UK Foreign Office says the Iranian Embassy requires an organised tour or a sponsor in Iran.

faq.question: Can I visit Iran if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says that if your passport has stamps from Israel or other countries' border crossing points with Israel, you may be refused entry to Iran. Canada's travel advice says Canadians have been denied entry because their passports bore an Israeli visa, an Israeli border stamp or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp issued by an office bordering Israel. No official page we could read states Iran's rule for Israeli passport holders; Iran's MFA visa portal says only that the citizens of some countries may not be issued a visa due to political and diplomatic considerations.

faq.question: Can I use my credit card in Iran?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says the economy is exclusively cash-based, credit cards are not accepted and ATMs serve only local bank accounts, and it advises bringing sufficient cash, preferably in US dollars or euros; the UK government adds that non-Iranian debit cards will not work.

faq.question: What is the dress code for women in Iran?
faq.answer: The UK government says Islamic dress codes are strictly enforced. In public places women must cover their heads with a headscarf and wear trousers or a floor-length skirt with a long-sleeved tunic or coat reaching mid-thigh or knee, and may be asked to wear a chador at religious sites. It also reports that the authorities have arrested and detained women for not following the dress code, and that enforcement crackdowns can happen at any time.

faq.question: Is Iran safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel. Australia's Smartraveller says do not travel to Iran and that foreigners, including dual nationals, are at high risk of arbitrary detention or arrest; the UK government says British and British-Iranian dual nationals face a very high risk of arrest, questioning and detention.
